factors.name: Size and branching complexity
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks, Average connector degree, Control flow complexity and Size load about 0.80–0.82, with Maximum connector degree (0.60) and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.56) as cross-loading members. The factor groups larger nets with more choice/parallel branching and more repeated or silent transition labels. Given the single dominant eigenvalue (6.25), it also acts much like a general complexity factor.

factors.name: Density (inverse)
factors.summary: Only Density is assigned, with a strong negative loading (-0.90), so the factor increases as nets become sparser relative to 2·|T|·|P|. Size (0.45), Maximum connector degree (0.43) and Control flow complexity (0.42) load moderately below threshold, consistent with density shrinking as nets grow. Being carried by one measure with a possible Heywood case, it may be little more than a split-off of the size dimension.

factors.name: Connectivity / arcs per node
factors.summary: Coefficient of network connectivity (0.71) and Maximum connector degree (0.48) define this factor, and both also cross-load on Factor 1. Average connector degree loads 0.44 here but is assigned only to Factor 1. It captures arc richness per node beyond overall size, but rests on two cross-loading measures.

factors.name: Separability
factors.summary: Only Separability loads clearly (0.69). Its communality is moderate (0.54), and the factor explains the least variance (12%). It seems to reflect how far the net lacks articulation points, a structural aspect largely separate from size, but rests on a single measure.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO (0.73) exceeds 0.6, so the data are suitable for factor analysis. However, the eigenvalues (6.25, 0.82, 0.53, …) and the suggested factor count of 1 indicate one dominant complexity dimension. Four varimax factors were extracted, explaining 91% of the variance. Factor 1 captures size and branching complexity. Factors 2–4 are each driven mainly by one or two measures (Density, connectivity, Separability) and should be read as minor facets rather than robust dimensions.
caveats: Four factors were retained although only one eigenvalue exceeds 1 and one factor was suggested, so Factors 2–4 are likely over-extracted.
Communalities at the bound for Size, Control flow complexity, Density and Number of duplicate tasks suggest a possible Heywood case, which makes the loadings less reliable.
Maximum connector degree and Coefficient of network connectivity cross-load on Factors 1 and 3, blurring the distinction between them.
Factors 2 and 4 each rest on a single measure.
Sequentiality and Connector Mismatch were removed by the MSA filter, and three measures were constant, so the factor structure does not cover these aspects.
The results depend on this dataset of 288 discovered nets, the varimax rotation and the chosen factor count, and do not imply causal relations.
